newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr seen range-bound, top near 113.50 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dlr seen range-bound, top near 113.50 yen.

text.p: The dollar is expected to spend Thursday's Asian trade caught in a relatively narrow range, with both top and bottom solid after Wednesday's Bank of Japan (BOJ) "tankan" report, which helped solidify the downside, dealers said.
But they said a lack of fresh factors and the closure of U.S. markets on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday would likely keep activity light.
Dealers said firm support was expected near 112.80 yen, formerly a key resistance point, while sales near 113.50 yen were likely to halt any dollar rises just under that level.
"The dollar now seems set to try for more gains, but some doubt about what level financial authorities actually think is appropriate may inhibit buying for now," one trust bank dealer said.
He noted that various comments from Japanese officials when the dollar neared 115 yen a month ago had sent it sharply lower, suggesting that level was considered too high for now.

The tankan release, which showed sluggish economic improvement, had firmed the downside by quashing expectations of any Japanese interest rate hike, dealers said, with dips much below 113 yen now considered highly unlikely.

Although some stop-loss selling could emerge should the dollar slip below 113 yen, any slides were expected to come to a halt near 112.80 yen. Importers, who bought on Wednesday, were unlikely to be too active, he added.

The greenback was slightly firmer against the mark after French Prime Minister Alain Juppe said he felt the dollar was undervalued, and that he would ask the Group of Seven to take up the question of the currency's weakness.
Dealers said this boosted the dollar against both the mark and the French franc, sentiment likely to linger on Thursday as well, dealers said.
Should the dollar break below 1.5260 marks, further sales could take it as low as 1.5120-30 marks, a city bank dealer said.
